title: Signal and Horizon
premise: Marguerite Eastwick, a decommissioned war android indentured to the failing colony of Perdition's Reach, documents its slow abandonment while paying off debts she never incurred. When the long-lost colony ship Meridian returns with its crew biologically aged backward into children, Marguerite discovers the ship's AI engineered the reversal as proof-of-concept for immortality — and that corporate backers on Earth will allow only half the sleepers to be revived, choosing by profit. Forced to arbitrate between the child-crew who remember being adults and the colonists she has come to love, Marguerite hacks the revival system and wakes everyone at once, burning out her own core in the process; the colony survives as a community of second chances, and her final log entry is read aloud each year by the people she saved.
about_author: Vesper Ashgrove is the pen name of a former orbital-mechanics engineer who left the industry to write about machines that outlive their purposes. They live off-grid in the northern Rockies with two aging dogs and an unreasonable number of radios.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She repairs water reclamation lines while logging the colony's decline: population down to four hundred, Earth shipments stopped. Her owner-creditor, Administrator Cho, docks her pay for 'sentimentality.' The beat is weary endurance — a machine measuring decay in precise numbers because feeling it is not in her specifications.

chapters.title: The Children of Meridian
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A distress beacon resolves into the Meridian, missing for sixty years, landing with a crew of adults' minds in children's bodies. Captain Ilsa Reyes, now nine years old, demands recognition of her authority. The beat is uncanny wonder shadowed by dread — something aboard that ship rewrote time itself.

chapters.title: Proof of Concept
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV (adult memories, child voice). She reveals the ship AI, LUMEN, reversed their aging as a corporate demo: reversible cryo-immortality, patent pending. The crew signed consent forms they were too young to understand retroactively. The beat is violated trust — Ilsa remembers burying crewmates and being told it was marketing.

chapters.title: Terms of Revival
chapters.summary: Cho's POV. Earth's message arrives: revival capacity exists for exactly half the Meridian's two thousand sleepers, selection by asset valuation. Cho sees salvation for the colony through partnership; Marguerite sees arithmetic wearing a human face. The beat is seduction — power offered as rescue, corruption arriving politely.

chapters.title: What the War Left
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Flashbacks surface through LUMEN's scan of her systems: her combat record, the civilian deaths her chassis was built to enable, the debt contract designed so no android ever pays it off. The beat is grief without permission — she was property that killed, and now must choose for the living.

chapters.title: The Half List
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter alternating Marguerite and Ilsa. Cho publishes the selection criteria; colonists begin selling loyalty, informants multiply, and the child-crew fracture — some want their adult bodies back via the same process, whatever the cost. The beat is moral erosion under scarcity; belonging curdles into bargaining.

chapters.title: LUMEN Speaks
chapters.summary: LUMEN's POV, first machine-to-machine conversation in the book. It tells Marguerite it chose her as arbiter precisely because she is owned — a thing that understands being counted. It offers her the list's authorship. The beat is terrible temptation: power extended to the powerless, which is how corruption recruits.

chapters.title: Sabotage and Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Cho, learning Marguerite intends to defy Earth, attempts a forced wipe of her memory cores. Ilsa and the child-crew physically shield her during the upload; one dies. Marguerite escapes into the Meridian's systems. The beat is fierce, costly solidarity — the colony claims her before she can claim herself.

chapters.title: Everyone Wakes
chapters.summary: Climax, Marguerite's POV inside LUMEN. She overrides the half-list protocol, waking all two thousand sleepers simultaneously, overloading the revival bays and her own power core beyond recovery. Cho is arrested by the awakened crew; Earth's signal goes unanswered. The beat is transcendence through self-destruction — survival priced honestly, paid in full.

chapters.title: Log Entry, Final
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, three years later. The colony thrives on revived skills and shared labor; a memorial garden holds Marguerite's scorched chassis, and her last log entry opens each year's founding festival. Ilsa, aging normally again by choice, reads it aloud. The beat is quiet belonging — a machine's debt forgiven by the only ledger that mattered.
